name: Ossuary Arms Memento Vivere OA-7 'Momento'
description:
A unique electromagnetic weapon that fires a round containing a compressed data packet — a BCI-readable message encoded in the round's electromagnetic signature that the target's neural interface involuntarily processes on impact. The round delivers both physical damage and an information payload that forces the target's BCI to display a pre-loaded message, image, or data burst.

Ossuary Arms designed the OA-7 as a conceptual weapon — the idea that violence can carry a message is as old as warfare, but the Momento literalizes it. An operator loads a data packet into each round alongside the conventional kinetic payload. When the round strikes a BCI-equipped target, the electromagnetic burst from the impact interfaces with their neural hardware and displays the encoded content whether they want to see it or not.

The weapon has found use in psychological warfare, where the content of the data payload is as important as the physical damage. Threats, warnings, demands, and even advertisements have been delivered via Momento round. The weapon has also been used to deliver malware to BCI systems — a round that hacks as it kills.
legality: Licensed as conventional weapon — data payload legality varies by content
specifications: caliber: 7.62mm with embedded electromagnetic data module effective_range: 50-600 meters rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic, 1 round per 2 seconds capacity: 8-round magazine weight: 4.8 kg power_source: Data encoding: pre-charged electromagnetic module per round
tactical_use: The Momento is deployed in psychological warfare and intelligence operations where the message is as important as the bullet. Operators pre-load rounds with ultimatums, intelligence data, or malware payloads, then engage targets at range. Even non-fatal hits deliver the data payload, meaning the weapon can be aimed at extremities to wound and deliver a message simultaneously. In intelligence operations, the OA-7 has been used to inject tracking malware into a target's BCI — shot, infected, and tracked, in a single engagement.
cultural_context: Ossuary Arms continues their philosophical approach to weaponry with the Memento Vivere — Latin for 'remember to live,' a counterpoint to their Memento Mori sniper rifle. The concept of a bullet carrying a message has captured the imagination of GLMZ's artistic and military communities alike. Some operators compose elaborate data payloads as a form of creative expression — the last thing a target sees is not a muzzle flash but a personally-crafted message from the person who shot them.
story_hooks: A series of Momento rounds have been recovered from non-fatal shootings across multiple tiers. Each round contains the same data payload — a countdown timer that is currently at 72 hours. Nobody knows what happens when it reaches zero, and the timer is displayed on every victim's BCI without their ability to dismiss it.

A black-hat hacker has begun selling pre-loaded Momento rounds containing BCI rootkit malware. A single non-fatal hit gives the buyer complete access to the target's neural interface. The rounds are being marketed to stalkers, corporate espionage operators, and worse.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular rifle with a distinctly medical or surgical aesthetic — all clean lines and purposeful geometry. The receiver appears almost anatomical, with subtle curves suggesting data flow rather than ballistics. The overall impression is of a precision instrument that happens to be lethal.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Barrel length: 51 cm | Width at receiver: 8 cm | Height with sights: 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly balanced despite its 4.8 kg mass — the weight feels distributed toward the user's natural shoulder pocket. Heavy enough to feel substantial and purposeful, light enough for precision work. The electromagnetic modules in each round add barely perceptible heft to the magazine.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite frame with brushed titanium alloy receiver and barrel jacket. The magazine housing is reinforced polymer with embedded conductive traces for data transmission.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents. The barrel jacket has a faint iridescent sheen from electromagnetic shielding. Receiver bears light surface wear from field use — small scratches that catch light, revealing underlying chrome.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed titanium silver accents. Deep matte black grip sections. Subtle violet bioluminescent trim around the data module chamber, visible only in dim light.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with fine crosshatch pattern — designed for sweaty or gloved hands. Slightly tacky, almost medical-grade texture. The magazine well has a smooth, almost slippery polymer coating for rapid reloads.
distinctive_features: Transparent data module window on the left receiver side — visible electromagnetic coil inside each chambered round
Thin violet LED status strip running along the top rail (armed/disarmed/data-loaded indicator)
Unusual charging handle with integrated touchpad for data programming
Heat vents along the barrel jacket arranged in precise geometric patterns
Serialized data encryption plate on the right side of receiver
Magazine shows individual round status — tiny LEDs marking data payload integrity
Minimalist iron sights with polarized glass for clarity at range
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Large 'OSSUARY ARMS' serif stamp on left receiver. 'MEMENTO VIVERE' engraved in elegant script below. Model designation 'OA-7' stamped on the barrel jacket. Small circled-Φ symbol (QUANTA currency mark) near the trigger guard — price per round encoding service. Serial number on underside of frame.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field weapon — pristine internal mechanisms, minimal corrosion. External finish shows light field wear: small scratches on the stock, faint fingerprint oils on the grip, occasional smudges on the data module window from gloved handling. No battle scarring; operators who field this weapon tend toward precision and preservation.
